Subject: Question: Private Offer pricing structure for Spectrum Health

Hi Sergio,

Quick question as we shape our AWS private offer: our procurement team is debating whether it's cleaner to anchor a single high list price and handle partner margin via a reseller netback, or to present explicit multi-line SKUs (base + partner fee) so the reseller margin is visible on invoices.

Primary asks:
- Which structure reduces invoicing friction for a hospital system that needs clear line items (tax, clinical vendor accounting)?
- Any implications for marketplace listing behavior and tax handling if we anchor at list vs split SKUs?
- We expect a 3-year committed spend (~$1.2M ARR) across us-east and us-west.

If you have a short matrix or recommendation (quick pros/cons and a sample margin number) that would help our legal and finance teams decide, that would be great.

Thanks — happy to jump on 30 mins if easier.

Alex Johnson
Head of Cloud Procurement
Spectrum Health

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Question: Private Offer pricing structure for Spectrum Health

Alex — thanks for the clear brief. Short answer: both approaches are valid; the best choice depends on downstream accounting and how the reseller expects to be paid. High-level guidance below, plus a quick template attached to illustrate the math.

Option 1 — Single list price (anchor) + reseller netback
- Pros: Simpler offer in the marketplace; one SKU to manage and faster checkout for customers.
- Cons: Reseller margin is off-invoice unless you include a separate rebate/payment flow; can be awkward for hospitals who need explicit line-item vendor fees.

Option 2 — Multi-line SKUs (base + partner fee)
- Pros: Clear line items for procurement and tax teams; reseller margin shows up directly on invoices.
- Cons: More SKUs to maintain; marketplace UI may split perceived price (higher cognitive load).

Questions that change recommendation:
1) Will your reseller (if any) invoice you directly, or do you need Redwood to pay them via passback?
2) Do you need explicit tax separation on the invoice?
3) Are you ok with an on-invoice partner fee showing as a third-party charge?

For a $1.2M 3-year commit, a typical starting point for partner economics is 10–15% netback at scale. If the reseller needs explicit line items for compliance, I’d recommend Option 2 with a base SKU + partner fee SKU and tiered discounts at commit thresholds. If you want fewer moving parts, Option 1 + an automated monthly passback (we can operationalize) will work.

I attached a small pricing_template.xlsx that runs the math for both approaches. Irene and Ben — looping you in for ops/tax and partner comp input; could you suggest recommended netback tiers and any operational caveats?

If this looks useful, I can draft a private-offer outline and a DocuSign-ready quote for Spectrum.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: pricing_template.xlsx

Sergio — quick ops notes:
- Option A: Redwood invoices the customer for the full list price. We then run a monthly passback to the reseller (recommended for non-US entities or when the reseller prefers settlement). Tax: Redwood is the billing party; customer sees a single charge. This keeps tax simpler for cases where Redwood collects and remits.
- Option B: Two line items on the invoice. If partner fee is charged as a Redwood line item, we need to ensure the reseller has the necessary tax docs (W-9 / local equivalents) on file; some hospital finance teams will insist on seeing the third-party vendor tax info.
- Invoice evidence: we can include a line-level description and an attached contract stub; sample_invoice_example.xlsx attached.
- Ops caveat: passback automation requires partner bank details and an MoU for settlement cadence (we have templates).

Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-25T11:12:00Z
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com

For reseller economics at this scale (>$1M), partners expect a baseline of 12% and will push for up to 16–18% with commit-based accelerators. Practical proposal: 12% standard netback, 15% if Spectrum signs a 3-year firm commit and hits the first-year ARR milestone (> $400k). If we present Option B (split SKUs), we should offer a slightly lower visible partner fee (11–12%) and make up the rest in an off-invoice rebate to avoid customer sticker shock.

My recommended deliverable: two short numbered options with Opex/CapEx language and a single-slide summary for procurement. Happy to take partner-facing comms.

(End forwarded thread)

Alex — thanks again. Based on your ask and internal ops/partner input, here are two concrete options to present to procurement. I pasted the short summary below and attached a draft private-offer PDF for review.

Summary (short):
Option A — Single list-price anchor + monthly passback (simpler invoice) - List price (3-year total): $1,200,000 (billed annually unless you prefer a different cadence) - Reseller netback: 14% of invoice value, paid monthly via automated passback to reseller bank account - Pros: one invoice line, Redwood handles tax/remittance; minimal finance friction for customers who want one charge - Cons: reseller margin not visible on customer invoice (we provide settlement statements)

Option B — Split SKUs: base + partner fee (explicit on invoice) - Base SKU (3-year total): $1,032,000 - Partner fee SKU (3-year total): $168,000 (equivalent to 14%) - Pros: partner fee visible on invoice for your accounting teams; easier for hospital vendor tracking - Cons: requires partner tax docs on file; marketplace entry has an extra SKU to maintain

Operational notes and next steps:
1) If you choose Option A we’ll prepare a clean private offer and automated passback schedule; passback will require reseller bank info and an MoU (Irene will send templates).
2) If you choose Option B we’ll collect partner tax documentation and prepare multi-line invoice templates (sample attached).
3) I’ve attached a draft private_offer_draft_v1.pdf and the pricing template so you can see the year-by-year math. If either option works, confirm and we’ll produce a DocuSign-ready quote (link included).

Would you like me to set up a 30-min call with our partner team to walk procurement and your reseller through the invoice and settlement flow?
